title: Catalog items API paging contract handoff
purpose: Document the two competing, unapproved drafts for the catalog items endpoint and the UI paging behavior they imply, so a human can pick the authoritative contract.

scope.text: Catalog API draft A: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string. UI must support moving to the next page.
Catalog API draft B: GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

requirements.text: Catalog API draft A: GET /v1/items returns a JSON object with an items array and next_cursor string.
UI must support moving to the next page.
Catalog API draft B: GET /v1/items returns a top-level JSON array and uses page and page_size query parameters.

stories.text: If a human selects draft A as the authoritative contract, a client can request the first page of catalog items and follow a next_cursor to move to the next page.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items succeeds, then the response body is a JSON object containing an items array and a next_cursor string.

Given a human has selected draft A as the authoritative contract and a response includes a next_cursor, when the UI requests the next page using that cursor, then the UI displays the next page of items.

stories.text: If a human selects draft B as the authoritative contract, a client can request a page of catalog items by supplying page and page_size query parameters.
acceptance_criteria: Given a human has selected draft B as the authoritative contract, when GET /v1/items is called with page and page_size query parameters, then the response body is a top-level JSON array of items.

dependencies.text: Neither draft is approved; the authoritative contract has not been selected.

risks.text: The drafts are incompatible: selecting draft A would leave the array-with-page-parameters shape from draft B unmet, and selecting draft B would leave the items-object-with-next_cursor shape from draft A unmet.

open_questions: Which draft should a human select as the authoritative contract for GET /v1/items: draft A or draft B?
Who has authority to select the authoritative contract?
